findings.finding: 30 ledger entries set conclusion_type=theorem while the ledger has no artifact_refs field at all. 25 of them are status=accepted. PROTOCOL.md rule 1 auto-rejects 'conclusion_type: theorem without artifact_refs', and the A0 rubric's HF-01 detector fires on exactly this pattern. Either artifact_refs must be added (locator + sha256 per entry) or the field must be renamed to something like mathematical_result_kind and the claim vocabulary reserved for claim events.

Internal contradiction between acceptance and verification: 4 entries are status=accepted with supports_claim=true while their own verification_status is 'unverified' (lines 1, 21, 24, 62; line 22 is provisional with the same flag). An entry cannot be accepted on evidence while its verification field says unverified. Either verification_status is defined on a different object than the entry (then it must be renamed and documented), or the acceptance is unjustified.

Evidence depth is below the G-LIT target: 45 of 49 accepted entries carry verification_status='abstract-read' and 30 accepted entries cite only registry sources whose status is 'verified-api' (metadata/abstract-level, no full-text primary read). Only 14 of 93 registry sources are verified-primary. citation_support == 1.0 (G-LIT criterion) is therefore not established for the accepted set.

Registry independence is nominal only: all 93 registry sources carry reviewer='lead-literature', so the registry's effective sample size is 1. Any citation_support metric computed over the 93 sources as if they were independent overstates support by up to 93x. Per the A0 metrics rule, report Kish ESS, never nominal n.

The artifact was revised after the assignment was written: the assignment evidence ref pins ledger/theorems.jsonl#4b21f12184c0, but the reviewed head is 5fb8bf3a. This review binds to 5fb8bf3a; the assignment's pinned prefix does not resolve to the reviewed content.
One entry is evidence_level='metadata-only' and is correctly marked provisional (line 61, D-009); no action, recorded for completeness.

positive_findings: All 62 entries carry non-empty source_ids and every referenced id resolves in the registry: the citation-resolution question passes cleanly.
No class_ids or informs_classes token falls outside the frozen four; no cross-class token was found.
No duplicate theorem_ids and no duplicate statement_exact hashes across the 62 entries, so HF-07 duplication is not present in the ledger itself.
No accepted entry relies solely on the single registry source with status 'unresolved'.
structure is regular: every entry carries assumptions, falsifiers, does_not_imply, scope_caveats, genericity, topology, regularity, unresolved, and next_action.
next_falsifier: If a re-run after adding artifact_refs (or renaming the theorem field) still leaves any accepted entry with verification_status='unverified', or if any accepted entry's only support remains verified-api after the literature group completes primary reads, the revise verdict stands and HF-01 remains open. Conversely, an entry-level diff showing artifact_refs on all 30 theorem entries and a registry ESS > 1 would justify re-review.
